findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission denied, or invalid path causes uncontrolled process abort instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and propagate the I/O error with ? or map_err

findings.failure_mode: Malformed line with non-numeric second field causes uncontrolled process abort instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use checked conversion or return Result with a typed ParseError via map_err

findings.problem: Lossy as cast from u32 to u16: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value outside u16 range (0..=65535) silently wraps, corrupting domain data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value) with proper error handling to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[0] without bounds check before access
findings.failure_mode: Line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes panic via index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract first two fields, or use get(0) and get(1) with Option handling

findings.problem: Uses split(',') + collect + indexed access instead of split_once(',')
findings.failure_mode: Allocates intermediate Vec<String> for every line (unnecessary heap allocation), and prevents the compiler from statically proving safe access
findings.fix: Replace with line.split_once(',') to get (name, rest) directly, then parse rest for the value

findings.problem: println! side-effect inside load_sessions which is a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Hidden I/O in a function that appears to be pure data transformation breaks functional-core purity, makes testing harder, and couples the core to a specific logger
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core; emit log messages at the shell layer after loading, or return a separate debug/trace structure

findings.problem: Function signature pub fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Vec<Record> has no error return type
findings.failure_mode: All fallible operations (file read, parse, bounds, cast) must panic since the caller cannot recover from any error — violates typed error contract
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: Value conversion from u32 (parse result) to u16 lacks range validation
findings.failure_mode: u32 values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16, producing incorrect domain data
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parts[1]) or parse directly to u16: parts[1].parse::<u16>().map_err(...) with proper error propagation

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocation for every line via .map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect()
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary per-line heap allocations for trimmed strings when split_once yields &str slices that can be used directly
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') on the line to get &str slices, then trim and parse directly without intermediate Vec<String>

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or latency
no profiler evidence for allocation hot spots in the parsing path
no allocation audit (no try_reserve, no allocation budget)
no second-ring evidence for claimed zero-allocation or low-latency behavior
no command-evidence from cargo check, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. All 9 findings are BLOCKER-level violations of Holzman Rust non-negotiables (unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy as, forbidden split+collect pattern, hidden I/O, missing error types, missing allocation safety). The crate would not compile under strict Holzman clippy gates and cannot ship until all forbidden constructs are eliminated and typed errors replace every panic point.
